items.note: The colour. The fruit is 'lemoen'.
'Goud' is the metal; 'goue' describes things.

items.exampleAf: Die baba se kamer is ligblou.
items.exampleEn: The baby's room is light blue.

items.note: Also the noun 'light' and 'light' in weight.

items.af: Hoewel die skildery net grys is, is dit vir my die mooiste.
items.en: Although the painting is only grey, it's my favourite.
wrongEn: Because the painting is only grey, I like it least.
Although the painting is only white, it's my favourite.
Although the painting has no grey in it, it's my favourite.
Although the painting is only grey, it's not my favourite.
wrongAf: Hoewel die skildery is net grys, is dit vir my die mooiste.
Hoewel die skildery net grys is, dit is vir my die mooiste.
Omdat die skildery net grys is, is dit vir my die lelikste.
Hoewel die skildery net wit is, is dit vir my die mooiste.
items.note: 'Hoewel' (although) sends 'is' to the end; the main clause then inverts: is dit.

items.af: Terwyl die son agter die berge verdwyn, word die lug pers.
items.en: While the sun disappears behind the mountains, the sky turns purple.
wrongEn: While the sun rises above the mountains, the sky turns purple.
While the sun disappears behind the mountains, the sky turns orange.
While the sun disappears behind the mountains, the sky stays blue.
Before the sun disappears behind the mountains, the sky turns pink.
wrongAf: Terwyl verdwyn die son agter die berge, word die lug pers.
Terwyl die son agter die berge verdwyn, die lug word pers.
Terwyl die son agter die berge verdwyn, word die lug oranje.
Terwyl die son agter die berge opkom, word die lug pers.
items.note: 'Terwyl' (while) sends 'verdwyn' to the end; the next clause starts with its verb: word die lug.

items.af: Die kunstenaar wie se skilderye so helder is, woon in Stellenbosch.
items.en: The artist whose paintings are so bright lives in Stellenbosch.
wrongEn: The artist whose paintings are so dull lives in Stellenbosch.
The artist whose paintings are so bright works in Stellenbosch.
The artist whose paintings are so bright lived in Stellenbosch.
The artist who lives in Stellenbosch paints in dull colours.
wrongAf: Die kunstenaar wat se skilderye so helder is, woon in Stellenbosch.
Die kunstenaar wie se skilderye is so helder, woon in Stellenbosch.
Die kunstenaar wie se skilderye so helder is, werk in Stellenbosch.
Die kunstenaar wie se skilderye so helder is, woon in die Paarl.
items.note: 'Wie se' = whose (for people). Not 'wat se'. The relative clause ends with its verb: is.

items.af: Die muurskildery is deur leerders van drie skole ontwerp en geverf.
items.en: The mural was designed and painted by learners from three schools.
wrongEn: The mural is being painted by learners from three schools.
The mural was designed and painted for learners from three schools.
The mural was designed and painted by learners from two schools.
Learners from three schools were painted in the mural.
wrongAf: Die muurskildery word deur leerders van drie skole ontwerp en geverf.
Die muurskildery het deur leerders van drie skole ontwerp en geverf.
Die muurskildery is deur leerders van drie skole geontwerp en geverf.
Die muurskildery is vir leerders van drie skole ontwerp en geverf.
items.note: Past passive with 'is' and 'deur' (by). Ontwerp starts with ont-, so it has no ge-; verf becomes geverf.

items.af: Juffrou het verduidelik dat ons groen kry as ons geel en blou meng.
items.en: The teacher explained that we get green if we mix yellow and blue.
wrongEn: The teacher explained that we get yellow if we mix green and blue.
The teacher asked whether we get green if we mix yellow and blue.
The teacher explained that yellow and blue don't make green.
The teacher explained that we get purple if we mix red and blue.
wrongAf: Juffrou het verduidelik dat ons kry groen as ons geel en blou meng.
Juffrou het verduidelik dat ons groen kry as ons meng geel en blou.
Juffrou het gevra of ons groen kry as ons geel en blou meng.
Juffrou het verduidelik dat ons geel kry as ons groen en blou meng.
items.note: A general truth stays in the present in reported speech. Both 'dat' and 'as' (if) send the verb last: groen kry, blou meng.

items.af: Nie een van die kinders het al ooit 'n wit renoster gesien nie.
items.en: Not one of the children has ever seen a white rhino.
wrongEn: Every one of the children has seen a white rhino.
One of the children has never seen a white rhino.
None of the children has ever seen a black rhino.
Not one of the children will ever see a white rhino.
wrongAf: Nie een van die kinders het al ooit 'n wit renoster gesien.
Nie een van die kinders het al ooit 'n wit renoster sien nie.
Een van die kinders het nog nooit 'n wit renoster gesien nie.
Nie een van die kinders sal ooit 'n wit renoster sien nie.
items.note: 'Nie een ... nie' = not one. The first 'nie' starts the subject, the second closes the sentence.

items.af: Sy het haar hare rooi gekleur en 'n groen rok by Ouma geleen.
items.en: She dyed her hair red and borrowed a green dress from Gran.
wrongEn: She dyed her hair red and lent a green dress to Gran.
She dyed her hair green and borrowed a red dress from Gran.
She will dye her hair red and borrow a green dress from Gran.
She cut her hair short and borrowed a green dress from Gran.
wrongAf: Sy het haar hare rooi gekleur en 'n groen rok aan Ouma geleen.
Sy het haar hare rooi kleur en 'n groen rok by Ouma leen.
Sy het haar hare groen gekleur en 'n rooi rok by Ouma geleen.
Sy gaan haar hare rooi kleur en 'n groen rok by Ouma leen.
items.note: One 'het' serves two past verbs: gekleur en geleen. 'By iemand leen' = borrow; 'aan iemand leen' = lend.

items.af: Jy mag nie aan die doek raak nie, aangesien vingers dit kan beskadig.
items.en: You may not touch the canvas, since fingers can damage it.
wrongEn: You may touch the canvas, since fingers cannot damage it.
You may not touch the canvas, since it can damage fingers.
You could not touch the canvas, since fingers had damaged it.
You may not touch the canvas, since fingers have damaged it.
wrongAf: Jy mag nie aan die doek raak, aangesien vingers dit kan beskadig.
Jy mag nie aan die doek raak nie, aangesien vingers kan dit beskadig.
Jy mag aan die doek raak, aangesien vingers dit nie kan beskadig nie.
Jy mag nie aan die doek raak nie, aangesien vingers dit gebeskadig.
items.note: 'Mag nie' = may not (not allowed). After 'aangesien' the modal and verb go last: kan beskadig. Doek = canvas.

items.af: Die nuwe onderwyser was net 'n blou Maandag by ons skool.
items.en: The new teacher was at our school for only a very short time.
wrongEn: The new teacher was at our school only on a sad Monday.
The new teacher was at our school for many years.
The new teacher only came to our school on Mondays.
The new teacher wore blue every Monday at our school.
wrongAf: Die nuwe onderwyser was jare lank by ons skool.
Die nuwe onderwyser was net op 'n Maandag by ons skool.
Die nuwe onderwyser was net 'n blou Dinsdag by ons skool.
Die nuwe onderwyser het net 'n blou Maandag by ons skool.
items.note: 'Net 'n blou Maandag' = only a very short time. It has nothing to do with the colour or the day.

items.af: Die herfsblare het soos goue munte in die son geblink.
items.en: The autumn leaves glittered in the sun like golden coins.
wrongEn: Golden coins glittered in the sun among the autumn leaves.
The autumn leaves faded in the sun like old paper.
The spring leaves glittered in the rain like golden coins.
The autumn leaves glittered in the moonlight like golden coins.
wrongAf: Die herfsblare het soos goue munte in die son blink.
Die herfsblare het soos goud munte in die son geblink.
Goue munte het tussen die herfsblare in die son geblink.
Die herfsblare het soos goue munte in die maanlig geblink.
items.note: A simile with 'soos'. Before a noun, 'goud' becomes 'goue': goue munte (golden coins).

items.af: Die see was 'n woedende grys monster wat die rotse bestorm het.
items.en: The sea was a furious grey monster that attacked the rocks.
wrongEn: A furious grey monster came out of the sea and attacked the rocks.
The sea was a calm grey blanket that covered the rocks.
The rocks were a furious grey monster that attacked the sea.
The sea was a furious green monster that attacked the boats.
wrongAf: Die see was 'n woedende grys monster wat die rotse het bestorm.
Die see was 'n woedende grys monster wat die rotse gebestorm het.
Die see was 'n woedende grys monster wat bestorm die rotse.
Die rotse was 'n woedende grys monster wat die see bestorm het.
items.note: A metaphor: the sea IS a monster (no 'soos'). Be- verbs take no ge-: bestorm het.

items.af: Eers nadat die verf droog was, het sy die skildery onderteken.
items.en: Only after the paint was dry did she sign the painting.
wrongEn: Even before the paint was dry, she signed the painting.
Only after the paint was dry did she frame the painting.
Only after she had signed the painting did the paint dry.
Only after the paint is dry will she sign the painting.
wrongAf: Eers nadat die verf droog was, sy het die skildery onderteken.
Eers nadat die verf was droog, het sy die skildery onderteken.
Eers nadat die verf droog was, het sy die skildery geonderteken.
Eers nadat die verf droog was, het sy die skildery verkoop.
items.note: A whole clause placed first counts as one position, so the verb comes next: het sy. Onderteken takes no ge-.

items.af: As die galery die skildery verseker het, sou hulle nie met leë hande gestaan het nie.
items.en: If the gallery had insured the painting, they would not have been left empty-handed.
wrongEn: Because the gallery had insured the painting, they were not left empty-handed.
If the gallery had insured the painting, they would have been left empty-handed.
If the gallery insures the painting, they will not be left empty-handed.
If the gallery had sold the painting, they would not have been left empty-handed.
wrongAf: As die galery die skildery verseker het, hulle sou nie met leë hande gestaan het nie.
As die galery die skildery geverseker het, sou hulle nie met leë hande gestaan het nie.
As die galery die skildery verseker het, sou hulle nie met leë hande gestaan het.
Omdat die galery die skildery verseker het, het hulle nie met leë hande gestaan nie.
items.note: Unreal past: as ... het, sou ... het. 'Met leë hande staan' = to be left empty-handed. Ver- verbs take no ge-.

items.af: Die rotsskilderye is eers onlangs beskryf, hoewel dit eeue gelede in oker aangebring is.
items.en: The rock art was only recently described, though it was made in ochre centuries ago.
wrongEn: The rock art was only recently made, though it was described centuries ago.
The rock art is only now being described, though it was made in ochre centuries ago.
The rock art was only recently described, though it was made in ochre a year ago.
The rock art was only recently described, because it was made in ochre long ago.
wrongAf: Die rotsskilderye het eers onlangs beskryf, hoewel dit eeue gelede in oker aangebring is.
Die rotsskilderye is eers onlangs gebeskryf, hoewel dit eeue gelede in oker aangebring is.
Die rotsskilderye is eers onlangs beskryf, hoewel dit is eeue gelede in oker aangebring.
Die rotsskilderye is eers onlangs aangebring, hoewel dit eeue gelede in oker beskryf is.
items.note: Two past passives: is beskryf, and aangebring is (verb last after 'hoewel'). Be- verbs take no ge-; aanbring: aangebring.

items.af: Die kleurpalet waarmee sy die Karoo vasvang, weerspieël 'n onbeskryflike eensaamheid.
items.en: The palette with which she captures the Karoo reflects an indescribable loneliness.
wrongEn: The palette with which the Karoo captures her reflects an indescribable loneliness.
The palette with which she captures the Karoo reflects an indescribable joy.
The palette with which she captures the Karoo hides an indescribable loneliness.
The palette she bought in the Karoo reflects an indescribable loneliness.
wrongAf: Die kleurpalet waarmee sy vasvang die Karoo, weerspieël 'n onbeskryflike eensaamheid.
Die kleurpalet waarvan sy die Karoo vasvang, weerspieël 'n onbeskryflike eensaamheid.
Die kleurpalet waarmee sy die Karoo vasvang, weerspieël 'n onbeskryflike vreugde.
Die kleurpalet waarmee die Karoo haar vasvang, weerspieël 'n onbeskryflike eensaamheid.
items.note: 'Waarmee' (with which) opens the relative clause; its verb goes last (vasvang), then the main verb: weerspieël.

items.af: Die kurator het gesê dat die doek weens sonlig vervaag het en gerestoureer sou word.
items.en: The curator said the canvas had faded because of sunlight and would be restored.
wrongEn: The curator asked whether the canvas had faded and could be restored.
The curator said the canvas had not faded and had already been restored.
The curator said the canvas had faded because of damp and would be replaced.
The curator said sunlight had brightened the canvas and it would be restored.
wrongAf: Die kurator het gesê dat die doek weens sonlig het vervaag en gerestoureer sou word.
Die kurator het gesê dat die doek weens sonlig vervaag het en restoureer sou word.
Die kurator het gevra of die doek weens sonlig vervaag het en gerestoureer kon word.
Die kurator het gesê dat die doek nie vervaag het nie en reeds gerestoureer is.
items.note: Reported speech: one past verb (vervaag het) and a future passive in the past (gerestoureer sou word).

items.af: Die resensent het geen blad voor die mond geneem nie: die uitstalling was smaakloos.
items.en: The reviewer did not mince his words: the exhibition was tasteless.
wrongEn: The reviewer did not hold a leaf before his mouth: the show was tasteless.
The reviewer chose his words carefully: the exhibition was tasteful.
The reviewer did not mince his words: the exhibition was superb.
The reviewer did not say a word: the exhibition was tasteless.
wrongAf: Die resensent het geen blad voor die mond geneem: die uitstalling was smaakloos.
Die resensent het geen blad voor die mond neem nie: die uitstalling was smaakloos.
Die resensent het sy woorde versigtig gekies: die uitstalling was smaakvol.
Die resensent het geen woord gesê nie: die uitstalling was smaakloos.
items.note: 'Geen blad voor die mond neem nie' = not to mince one's words. 'Geen ... nie' closes with 'nie'.

items.af: Die herfs het die wingerde goud geverf, asof die natuur 'n meesterstuk wou voltooi.
items.en: Autumn painted the vineyards gold, as if nature wanted to finish a masterpiece.
wrongEn: Autumn painted the vineyards gold, because nature had finished a masterpiece.
Someone painted the vineyards gold to finish a masterpiece.
Winter painted the vineyards white, as if nature wanted to finish a masterpiece.
Autumn stripped the vineyards bare, as if nature wanted to destroy a masterpiece.
wrongAf: Die herfs het die wingerde goud geverf, asof die natuur wou 'n meesterstuk voltooi.
Die herfs het die wingerde goud geverf, asof die natuur 'n meesterstuk wou gevoltooi.
Die herfs het die wingerde goud verf, asof die natuur 'n meesterstuk wou voltooi.
Die herfs het die wingerde goud geverf, omdat die natuur 'n meesterstuk voltooi het.
items.note: Personification: autumn paints and nature is an artist. 'Asof' (as if) sends 'wou voltooi' to the end.

items.af: Nêrens in die land sal jy blomme sien wat met Namakwaland s'n vergelyk kan word nie.
items.en: Nowhere in the country will you see flowers that compare with Namaqualand's.
wrongEn: Everywhere in the country you will see flowers that compare with Namaqualand's.
Nowhere in Namaqualand will you see flowers that compare with the rest of the country's.
Nowhere in the country did you see flowers that compared with Namaqualand's.
Somewhere in the country you will see flowers that beat Namaqualand's.
wrongAf: Nêrens in die land jy sal blomme sien wat met Namakwaland s'n vergelyk kan word nie.
Nêrens in die land sal jy blomme sien wat kan met Namakwaland s'n vergelyk word nie.
Nêrens in die land sal jy blomme sien wat met Namakwaland s'n vergelyk kan word.
Oral in die land sal jy blomme sien wat met Namakwaland s'n vergelyk kan word.
items.note: 'Nêrens' placed first causes inversion (sal jy). The relative clause ends 'vergelyk kan word', then 'nie'.

items.af: Nadat die vergeelde vernis verwyder is, het die oorspronklike kleure na vore gekom.
items.en: After the yellowed varnish had been removed, the original colours emerged.
wrongEn: After the yellow varnish had been applied, the original colours were lost.
Before the yellowed varnish was removed, the original colours emerged.
After the yellowed varnish had been removed, the colours looked dull.
Once the yellowed varnish is removed, the original colours will emerge.
wrongAf: Nadat die vergeelde vernis is verwyder, het die oorspronklike kleure na vore gekom.
Nadat die vergeelde vernis verwyder is, die oorspronklike kleure het na vore gekom.
Nadat die vergeelde vernis geverwyder is, het die oorspronklike kleure na vore gekom.
Voordat die vergeelde vernis verwyder is, het die oorspronklike kleure na vore gekom.
items.note: A passive 'nadat' clause first (verwyder is), then the main clause inverts: het die kleure. 'Na vore kom' = emerge.
